questions.question: Which command creates a new Django app named blog?
questions.explanation: startapp generates an application package skeleton.

questions.question: By convention, which file maps URL patterns to views?
questions.explanation: urls.py holds urlpatterns that route URLs to views.

questions.question: Which command generates migration files from model changes?
questions.explanation: makemigrations writes migration files; migrate applies them.

questions.question: Which command creates a user who can log into the Django admin with all permissions?
questions.explanation: createsuperuser creates a user with is_staff and is_superuser set.

questions.question: Which ORM call returns a QuerySet of all Book objects?
questions.explanation: The default manager objects provides all().

questions.question: Which Django template syntax outputs the value of a variable name?
questions.explanation: {{ }} outputs variables; {% %} is used for tags.

questions.question: Which setting lists the applications enabled in a Django project?
questions.explanation: Apps must be listed in INSTALLED_APPS for models, templates and migrations to be found.

questions.question: Which model field is meant for short strings and renders as a single-line text input in forms?
questions.explanation: CharField is for short strings; TextField is for large text and renders as a textarea.

questions.question: What does Book.objects.get(pk=999) do if no such row exists?
questions.explanation: get() raises the model's DoesNotExist exception when nothing matches.

questions.question: Which QuerySet method avoids N+1 queries on a ForeignKey by using a SQL JOIN?
questions.explanation: select_related follows forward foreign keys in the same query using a JOIN.

questions.question: For a ManyToManyField, which method loads related objects in a separate query and joins them in Python?
questions.explanation: prefetch_related issues an extra query per relation and does the joining in Python.

questions.question: When does qs = Book.objects.filter(x=1) first hit the database?
options: When save() is called on a Book
When the QuerySet is evaluated, e.g. iterated or passed to list()
questions.explanation: QuerySets are lazy and run their SQL only when evaluated.

questions.question: Which construct lets you combine filter conditions with OR?
questions.explanation: Q objects can be combined with | and & to build complex lookups.

questions.question: What does Product.objects.filter(pk=1).update(stock=F("stock") - 1) achieve?
options: Loads the row into Python, decrements, then saves
Decrements stock in a single SQL UPDATE, avoiding a read-modify-write race
Creates a new field named stock
questions.explanation: F() references the column value in the database, so the arithmetic happens in SQL.

questions.question: Which template tag must appear inside a POST form for Django's CSRF protection to accept it?
questions.explanation: {% csrf_token %} renders the hidden token checked by CsrfViewMiddleware.

questions.question: Which generic class-based view is designed to display a list of objects?
questions.explanation: ListView renders a page representing a list of objects.

questions.question: What does wrapping code in transaction.atomic() guarantee?
options: Database operations in the block are committed together or rolled back together if an exception escapes
The block runs under a process-wide thread lock
Query results in the block are cached
questions.explanation: atomic opens a transaction (or savepoint) that is rolled back if the block raises.

questions.question: Which QuerySet method locks the selected rows until the end of the current transaction?
questions.explanation: select_for_update issues SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and must run inside a transaction.

questions.question: What does Author.objects.annotate(n=Count("books")) produce?
options: A single dict with the total number of books
A new database column n on the author table
A QuerySet where each Author has attribute n with its own book count
Only the authors that have no books
questions.explanation: annotate adds a per-object aggregate, computed with GROUP BY.

questions.question: Where should signal handlers be connected so they register once when Django starts?
questions.explanation: ready() runs once the app registry is loaded; importing signals there avoids side effects and duplicates.

questions.question: In which order does middleware process the response, relative to the MIDDLEWARE list?
options: In reverse order, from bottom to top
In the same order, from top to bottom
questions.explanation: Requests pass through middleware top-down and responses bottom-up, like layers of an onion.

questions.question: Which method inserts many objects efficiently but does not call save() or send pre_save/post_save signals?
questions.explanation: bulk_create inserts in few queries and bypasses save() and the save signals.
